name: core-schedules
description: Schedules on a table beside its Workflow, D104: setSchedule arms a schedule after a delay, at an interval or on a cron line in a time zone, bounded by minMs and maxMs, at most max of them live; a due one fires on the worker as the deadline it armed, records its run, emits the event run and arms the next from the time it fired, so an overdue one fires once; a cron line's local time a daylight-saving change skips runs at the gap's first instant, its first minute among them, and one it repeats runs once; pause, resume and cancel; a replace and a finished name set again count the name's runs on; reportRun records an outcome and the retry outcome tries the run again as its next attempt, and a late report of an earlier attempt or of a replaced schedule's run changes nothing; endOn finishes a row's schedules when its Workflow enters a listed state, through a transition and through a raw write its change queue carries; finished schedules beyond max go; a new version's narrower config holds new sets alone; with each one's define refusals. Cases written by hand in the recorded format, since no engine implements Schedules. Each answer holds what the replayer compares: a record's id, data and behaviors, an operation's result, a refusal whole, in the core's words, and the events each step's commands wrote (events); what only the engine's store answers (sequence numbers, versions, timestamps, the document a define echoes) is left out.
